system_architecture.description: CSF shunt valve whose opening pressure profile adapts to ICP trend rather than fixed cracking pressure; reduces postural pressure excursions

subsystems.name: Adaptive valve seat
subsystems.function: Variable-area flow orifice whose area A(P, dP/dt) depends on pressure and pressure trend

subsystems.name: Pressure-trend sensor
subsystems.function: Measures ICP(t) and computes dP/dt for controller input

subsystems.name: Actuator (candidate: MEMS electrothermal or shape-memory polymer)
subsystems.function: Adjusts valve seat area based on controller signal

subsystems.name: Controller (P or PI)
subsystems.function: Maps (P, dP/dt) -> actuator command to track target opening profile

fluid_mechanics.flow_regime: Laminar (CSF Re << 2300 at shunt flow rates ~0.3 mL/min in 1-1.5 mm ID catheter)
fluid_mechanics.pressure_range: ICP 5-20 mmHg normal, postural transients to 40 mmHg reported
key_equations: Q = (pi * r^4 * dP) / (8 * eta * L)  [laminar flow through circular conduit]
Q = Cd * A * sqrt(2 * dP / rho)     [turbulent/orifice flow]
Re = (rho * v * D) / eta             [laminar if Re < 2300]
fluid_mechanics.critical_parameter: Valve conductance G(P, dP/dt) = Q / dP, intentionally variable vs fixed

dual_invariants.INV-1: P_ICP <= 20 mmHg (intracranial pressure safety; same threshold class as P-01 — MODEL_DERIVED per R332)
dual_invariants.INV-2: Q_drainage >= 0.05 mL/min (minimum drainage floor; prevents overdrainage-induced collapse AND underdrainage)

mechanism_architecture.physical_changes: Valve orifice area A adapts: when dP/dt indicates postural transient (positive trend with postural change), the valve reduces conductance briefly to attenuate over-drainage; when ICP rises monotonically, conductance increases to maintain drainage.
mechanism_architecture.key_physics: Variable-area orifice: Q = Cd * A(dP, dP/dt) * sqrt(2 dP / rho). The 'adaptive' component is the A(dP, dP/dt) dependence — a non-linear feedback on the orifice equation.

trend_estimator.model: Discrete derivative dP/dt with low-pass filter (cutoff < 0.1 Hz to reject pulsatile cardiac component)
trend_estimator.prediction_horizon: Not applicable — adaptive response is reactive, not predictive
trend_estimator.status: MODELLED — controller architecture specified; hardware transfer function UNKNOWN

governing_model.summary: Variable-area hydraulic orifice with trend-feedback control. The valve is modeled as a non-linear orifice whose area A is a function of measured pressure and its time-derivative.
equations: Q = Cd * A * sqrt(2 * dP / rho)     [turbulent/orifice flow]
Q = (pi * r^4 * dP) / (8 * eta * L)  [laminar flow through circular conduit]
Re = (rho * v * D) / eta             [laminar if Re < 2300]
A_actuator(P, dP/dt) = A0 + k_p * (P - P0) + k_d * dP/dt   [proposed controller law, MODELLED]
assumptions: CSF is Newtonian (valid at low shear rates in shunt flow)
Flow is quasi-steady (valve response time > flow timescale)
No cavitation (validated by Re and pressure range)
boundary_conditions: Outlet: intra-abdominal pressure ~5-15 mmHg supine, lower upright
Postural head differential: 0-50 cm H2O (~0-37 mmHg)
parameter_sensitivities: A_actuator gain k_p -> directly controls response amplitude
Filter cutoff frequency -> determines pulsatile rejection vs response lag
failure_regimes: Actuator saturation (max area reached) -> reverts to fixed-valve behavior
Filter lag > postural transient duration -> adaptation ineffective
Sensor noise > dP/dt signal -> controller unstable

engineering_core.external_precedent: EXTERNAL_PRECEDENT ≠ INVENTION_VALIDATION — see external_engineering_precedent field for FDA-cleared comparable valves (Miethke proGAV, Medtronic Strata). These establish that programmable shunt valves are manufacturable. They do NOT establish that the adaptive profile proposed here achieves clinical benefit.

proposed_design.mechanism: Trend-feedback controller modulates valve seat area
proposed_design.transformation: (P, dP/dt) -> A_actuator -> Q(P, A) -> drainage rate
proposed_design.output: Drainage rate that attenuates postural excursions while maintaining minimum floor
proposed_design.component_architecture: Pressure sensor -> controller (MCU) -> actuator -> variable valve seat -> outlet catheter
